properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/28/2026
Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8286893
Permit API: 051-22973
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/28/2026
Comments: On 8/28/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Orr 14 OG well in Washington Township, Fayette County.The inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, received on 8/25/2026.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- The access road appears to be a multi-use road that is shared with additional Diversified well sites. Evidence of minor stormwater washout was observed in portions of the shared access road at the time of inspection. The well site is located within a forested agricultural area. Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed downslope of the well site. The area surrounding the well site is heavily saturated, with evidence of heavy animal traffic observable at the time of inspection. The E and S/Restoration plan was not located on site during this inspection. However, the E and S/Restoration plan was located during a Department SubSurface inspection (IR 4266229) that overlaps the time of this inspection.- The gas well is equipped with a well tag. No additional equipment related to well plugging and/or production was observed on site during this inspection. The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was not observed on site.- While on site, the Department spoke with Ed from Glade Pipeline Services, who confirmed that third-party disturbances are occurring at the well site due to livestock grazing, and explained that they were on site to make repairs on the access road and the well site.- Upon exiting the site toward Connellsville Street, the Department observed loose soil that had been pushed adjacent to an apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run during today's aforementioned access road repairs (Photos 17-20). Although no sediment was observed entering this apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run at the time of inspection, it is actively under threat by this site since no E and S control measures are installed in this location. The Department recommends that the operator take immediate action to cease ongoing threats to the Waters of the Commonwealth.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures prior to conducting earth disturbances on the access road, which is resulting in a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending review of the site E and S plan in a subsequent surface inspection.An additional violation will be issued in IR 4265922 for failure to post the Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) on site.While on site, the Department notified Diversified representative Daniel Frick via voicemail of the Department's observations and forthcoming violations from this inspection and IR 4265922.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a66(b)2 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to contact the appropriate regional Department office by telephone or call the Department’s Statewide toll free number as soon as practicable, but no later than 2 hours after discovering the spill or release.
Violation ID: 948137
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/16/2022
Comments: On March 16, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline and Brooke Millisock conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The DEP observed and sampled five seeps and four stream sites that were found off the west side of the well pad in "Deep Hollow" along an UNT to Rattlesnake Run. STL Resources revealed that the seeps were occurring and being monitored for specific conductivity and chlorides on March 1, 2022 during a meeting with the DEP. The data that STL Resources provided showed levels of elevated conductivity in seeps 1, 1A, and 4. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling site for pH and conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 had a pH of 8.61 and conductivity of 29.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 had pH of 7.97 and a conductivity of 29.8 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 had pH of 7.18 and a conductivity of 22.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 had a pH of 6.84 and a conductivity of 22.2. Seep 1 had a pH of 5.14 and a conductivity of 308 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a pH of 5.04 and a conductivity of 345 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a pH of 6.62 and a conductivity of 43.2 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a pH of 6.3 and a conductivity of 42.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a pH of 6.25 and a conductivity of 191.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had pH of 8.01 and a conductivity of 28.2 uS/cm. Water quality samples 0651-104, 106, 108, and 111 were collected at the four stream sampling sites and submitted for SAC code 942 plus Aluminum, Lithium, and Bromide. Water quality samples 0651-105, 107, 109, and 110 were collected at seeps 1,1A, 4, and 5. Water quality sample 0651-112 was collected in a channel downgradient of Seeps 2 and 3 due to not enough water available to sample in these seeps. An additional seep was observed up the logging road of Seep 3, this seep had pH of 6.67 and conductivity of 22.5. The previously mentioned seep did not appear to be monitored by STL Resources. The southwest infiltration berm excavation area remains uncovered and the stormwater level in the area as begun to recede eliminating the overflowing of the area. The water level in the southwest stormwater vault was about a foot deep and was unable to be screened for conductivity. The water level in the northwest stormwater vault was about 18 inches and could not be screened for conductivity. The seeps that were observed near the northwest stormwater vault on March 3, 2022 were not flowing at the time of inspection. A new area of excavation was observed where the water from these seeps was pooling. This area has been covered with a tarp. There was water pooled on top of the tarp and next to the tarp. The conductivity of this water was 3,400 uS/cm. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources said they will continue to vacuum the pooling water as necessary. The pooled water in this area could be seen overflowing into an adjacent depression that was covered with a tarp. The DEP recommends exploring this area and removing any contaminated water and soil. STL Resources has removed the contaminated soil stockpile that was being staged on the well pad. Well Pad remediation from the spill that occurred on January 8, 2022 has not occurred. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Unconventional: No

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an active stray gas migration investigation. Methane was detected on the outside of the surface casing and an attempt was made to plug the well. During the plugging process several joints of tubing were accidentally cemented in the well. A camera was ran in the well and bubbles were seen at the top of the fluid. An MSA Altair 5X gas detector detected methane in the well bore. A violation for improper plugging was issued. The cement will be drilled out to approximately 550' which is 50' below the surface casing shoe. The 1.5" tubing will have to be removed in order to accomplish this. Todays operations: Big Run rig 118 began drilling with a 4" core bit on a power swivel at 340.88'. Ending depth for the day was 355.88'.

Comments: I conducted a routine inspection of the Allshouse Fraser 1001 well, this well was stimulated yesterday. The road surface did not hold up to the increased traffic as heavy mud and significant ruts are present. Accelerated erosion of the road surface is taking place, a spring run with steady flow is present and running down the road due to lack of a culvert or other BMP to carry the water across the road. The water then ran an additional 200 feet over the hillside and into the storm drain on the east bound lane of Route 6. From there the sediment laden water continued to the storm sewer outfall above the river and entered into the Allegheny River. The plume of sediment water remained for approximately 30 feet along the south bank of the Allegheny River.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a FUI inspection at the Tilden Marcellus LLC - Pierson 801 located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 10/2/2019 @0845 hours. The weather was sunny 74 degrees. Onsite for the inspection was myself, Korey Starkey, DEP WQS; Jennifer Compton and Nathan Smelser, Tilden Marcellus; Farmer Boy Restoration; Civil and Environmental Consultants, Inc.(CEC) As of today's inspection, a large stain was observed on the gravel surface adjacent to the failed dump line measuring ~8'x4'(See Photo#1). Tilden's earthmoving sub-contractor, Farmer Boy Restoration, had used a small excavator to scrape the surface of the impacted pad area, fill slope (see photo #2) and dig a sump in the fill slope approximately 4' wide and 5' deep. Fluid that had accumulated in the bottom of the sump had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm(See Photo#3). Sample 4427-192 was collected from the fluid in the fill slope sump and submitted to the DEP laboratory in Harrisburg for SAC 942 analysis. CEC consultants had delineated the extent of the impacted area with white flags. The excavator, and CEC, were currently working to remove soil with an elevated conductivity in an area below the toe of the fill slope(See Photo#4,5). The excavated sump was then expanded across the fill slope. A wet gravel layer was observed ~3' below the pad surface that appeared to be the source of the >19.99mS/cm fluid entering the sump(See Photo#6). Jennifer Compton and CEC continued to screen the fill slope area and remove additional material. The impacted material was being staged on the pad surface, on the interior of the gas line, awaiting the delivery of more disposal boxes. Ms. Compton was also awaiting the delivery of a super sucker truck to remove additional pad material. Tilden Marcellus and CEC were advised to contact the DEP Environment Cleanups and Brownfields (ECB) Program to facilitate cleanup activities going forward. Violations cited previously in inspection report#2939891, dated 9/30/2019 are cited as OUTSTANDING against the 2H well, API#117-20309 at this time. We departed the site @1200 hours.

Comments: On 12/18/2025, an incident inspection was conducted at the John Briggs Well pad in Aleppo Township, Greene County for a reported release (CTS: 394097). I was accompanied by DEP Water Quality Specialist Sara Trio.The spill was reported to the Department by the operator on 12/11/2025 through the DEP Emergency Hotline. It was reported that the piping inside the 50U Gas Processing Unit (GPU) washed out and produced fluids spilled off containment and onto the well pad. The amount reported was greater than 5 gallons and the spill was contained to the well pad. Specialized Professional Services, Inc (SPSI) was on site the same day to begin clean up.The following was observed during the inspection:- The spill area was observed adjacent to the 50U GPU. The impacted gravel was excavated. Absorbent material was observed behind the GPU (Photos 1-3).- Conductivity readings were taken throughout the spill area. Elevated conductivity was observed in two small holes sumps that collected fluids (Photos 4-6). Elevated conductivity was also observed behind the GPU near the absorbent material (Photo 7).- Additional conductivity readings were taken throughout and outside of the spill area. They were all observed to be below clean up standards (Photos 8-12).It appears the spill still needs additional remediation in certain areas. The Department requests information on the amount spilled and how the amount was verified.Violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued for the spill.

Violations issued in IR 4165270 for PCSM BMPs not maintained by operator are being corrected at this time.Violations issued in IR 4165270 are being continued for the sedimentation observed along the access road.

An additional reading was taken on the side closest to the well at the former brine tank location, but approximately 6 inches of soil was dug before the reading was taken. It read .38 Micro Siemens. A background reading was taken 50 feet west of the well which read .24 Micro Siemens (see photo 9). Overall, the conductivity of the soil at the site of the possible brine release appears to now be comparable to the surrounding soil.Based on observations from today's inspection, the impacted soil appears to have been removed as of August 26, 2022. Comments: Onsite for a routine inspection. The well is equipped with a pump jack, rods, and tubing. The pump jack does not have a motor/engine or belt to operate the well. The surface casing is vented and the well is labeled with a metal sign near the well. Tank Battery: It was noted in the previous site inspection, Inspection Report # 3198057 dated 5/26/2021; that one of the 210bbl steel tanks were showing signs of corrosion and weeping fluid. The steel tank has been replaced with a 100bbl poly tank. The old steel tank remains onsite along the access road/well site. The poly tank is full with brine water and the bulkheads are leaking fluid to the earthen dike. The area around the tank is wet. The dike drain is open and continuously discharging (dripping) fluid to the ground. There is a visual impact area downslope of the open dike drain. The impact area extends 40-50' from the drain pipe. Fluid from the dripping drain pipe was collected and field tested. The field screening indicates that the fluid is brine water with conductivity readings of 4,470 uS. The discharge of brine to the ground is an unlawful act. The Department requests that the operator make repairs to the tank and remediate the impacted area according to state regulations and policies for spills/releases on oil and gas well sites. Violation(s) are cited.

properties.content:
Report Details
Operator Cabot Oil &Amp; Gas Corp
Violation Type Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date 2016-07-22
Violation Code CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID 764968
Permit API 115-20950
Unconventional Y
County Susquehanna
Municipality Dimock Twp
Inspection Type Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date 2016-07-22
Comments Steve Watson, Environmental Health and Safety Specialist of Cabot Oil and Gas, contacted me at 8:36 AM on 7/22/16 to report a spill of (200) gallons of a mixture of recycled water and freshwater on the well pad off containment. Mr. Watson stated the following information. “The spill occurred in the Southeast corner of the well pad. Keane was in the process of fracking the 3H well when the spill occurred. A mixture of (25%) recycled water and (75%) freshwater overtopped a (55) gallon drum as part of an air vent tied to a transfer line. The line runs from the tank pad to the well pad. A blue disc made of plastic got sucked up into the fluid hose inside the drum. The disc got stuck above the ball valve in the air vent valve as water was flowing in the transfer line. This caused the water to flow into the hose and out of an opening on the top of the drum, onto the ground. The water flowed out of the drum and onto the ground for 4 or 5 minutes until it was discovered around 7AM. The valve on the air vent was shut immediately upon discovery of the spill. A backhoe and a roll-off container are there now. There is standing water on the pad. Resource Environmental is on their way. They will screen the area on the well where the spill occurred for conductivity and collect samples. The recycled water is brought to the site from Comtech. The fresh water is brought to the site from water withdrawals. Cabot will seek Act 2 Relief of Liability." I arrived at the site at 11:45 hours to investigate the incident and conduct an inspection of the site. I met with Mr. Watson on the tank pad of the site as I arrived. I also met with Andy Rodriguez, site Company Man, completions consultant of Cabot, Tony Maury, Account Manager of Rain for Rent, Steve Catalfamo and John Corbin of Resource. Cabot submitted a stimulation notice to the Department on 7/13/16 indicating that stimulation of the 3H well would commence on 7/18/16 at 7AM. Keane is currently in the process of conducting hydraulic fracturing operations on the H Petersen 3H well. The 12th stage was completed as of 7:25 AM, with this stage commencing at 5:15 AM according to Mr. Maury. Mr. Maury further stated that Cabot is in between frac stages and not currently pushing water through the transfer line and into the well. The impacted area where the spill occurred in the SE corner of the pad is next to the well pad perimeter berm at the top of the fill slope. A backhoe is being used to remediate the impacted area. A Diaz roll-off container covered with a liner made of plastic material is staged next to the backhoe. Mr. Watson informed me that the remediation process commenced sometime between 10:45-11:00 on 7/22/16. Thus far, (1) container of impacted material has been filled. The container is staged on the tank pad awaiting disposal via rail to Tunnel Hill Reclamation Landfill in Ohio. Resource is currently in the process of performing soil conductivity screening in the impacted area. The intent of the screening is to determine the extent of the excavation. Resource recorded (35) milliSiemens/cm³ conductivity in pooled fluid, and conductivity in the range of (300-1,000) microSiemems/cm³ on the surface of the impacted area. The depth of the excavation is (1) to (1.5) feet according to Resource. I used a Hanna HI 98331 Soil Test Electrical Conductivity and Temperature Meter to record soil conductivity in moist soil in (3) separate areas in the excavation. Conductivity was (940) µs/cm³ next to the excavator bucket, (340) µs/cm³ in between the bucket and the sidewall of the excavation near the perimeter berm, and (140) µs/cm³ near the sidewall of the excavation relatively close to the liner and equipment used for frac operations. Potential for pollutional substances to enter the waters of the commonwealth.

Comments: On April 26, 2024, inspection conducted at the former location of the Corbett 3 well site in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. Plugging was completed on November 8, 2022. No responses of any kind to violations issued under IR 3649965 have been received by the Department from the operator as of the time of this inspection. Present at this inspection were DEP Environmental Trainee Tori LaBirt and myself.The following was observed:The majority of the former well site location exhibits less than 70 percent uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage at the time of this inspection, and it appears that debris from production and/or plugging was left behind. The former access road location appeared to be stable at the time of inspection and exhibits at least 70 percent uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage. No restoration plans or E and S BMP's were found onsite.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite by the operator since the time of IR 3668503 when the Department was last onsite. Therefore, violations continued under IR 3668503 shall remain outstanding.
